BecomeHam.title: How to become a radio amateur
BecomeHam.intro: Since 25 August 2026 there is no minimum age and no waiting period. You sit the ANACOM exam, and you can move up a category as soon as you feel ready.

changed.title: Lei n.º 22/2026 amended Decreto-Lei n.º 53/2009.
changed.age: The minimum age is gone. Anyone may register for the exam. Minors need written authorisation from whoever holds parental responsibility or guardianship.
changed.wait: The permanence periods are gone. You no longer have to wait in category 3 before sitting the category 2 exam, or in category 2 before sitting category 1.
changed.licence: Individual stations no longer need a licence, and the CAN is now valid for 10 years.

BecomeHam.categoriesIntro: They are no longer separated by age or waiting time — they are separated by what they let you do on air.

category3.name: Category 3
category3.bands: Segments of 80, 40, 20 and 10 m, plus 6 m, 2 m and 70 cm
category3.power: 10 W on HF · 100 W on 10 m · 50 W on VHF/UHF

category2.name: Category 2
category2.bands: Wider access on HF, VHF and UHF, including 2 m satellite
category2.power: 200 W on HF · 150 W on VHF/UHF

category1.name: Category 1
category1.bands: Every band allocated to the amateur service
category1.power: 1500 W on HF · 300 W on VHF/UHF

BecomeHam.bandsIntro: Maximum peak power, in watts, on the bands in everyday use.
BecomeHam.bandsCaption: Maximum permitted power by frequency band and amateur category.
BecomeHam.bandsNote: Always use the minimum power needed for the contact — these are ceilings, not targets. The 145.806 – 146 and 435 – 438 MHz segments belong to the amateur-satellite service: this is where you work satellites and the ISS. The 2200 m, 630 m and 4 m bands, and the microwave allocations above 1240 MHz, are category 1 only and appear in Annex 6 of the QNAF. This table is about transmitting: receiving needs no privileges, so any category may listen on any band.
BecomeHam.progressionTitle: The order stays, the waiting does not
BecomeHam.progressionIntro: You still climb 3 → 2 → 1, because each exam requires the category below it. What disappeared was the clock between the steps.
BecomeHam.progressionNoGate: There are no minimum permanence periods. Pass all three exams in the same year and you move up all three categories in the same year.
BecomeHam.ageIntro: It now only affects operating. They are separate things, and this is where the confusion usually starts.

certificate.label: To earn the CAN
certificate.headline: Any age
certificate.body: There is no minimum age to sit the exam. If the candidate is a minor, written authorisation is required from whoever holds parental responsibility or guardianship under civil law.

operate.label: To operate
operate.headline: Under-16s supervised
operate.body: A category 3 CAN holder under 16 may only use amateur stations under the supervision of an amateur aged 16 or over holding privileges equal to or greater than their own.

registration.title: Register with ANACOM
registration.description: Fill in ANACOM's online form and pay the exam fee. If you are a minor, attach the written authorisation.

preparation.title: Prepare
preparation.description: Study the official syllabus with real exam questions, quick drills and flashcards.

exam.title: Written theory paper
exam.description: Attend at the venue ANACOM assigns, with photo ID. The paper is multiple choice, with a penalty for wrong answers.

licence.title: CAN and callsign
licence.description: You receive the certificate, valid for 10 years, and your callsign. An individual station no longer needs a licence — you can start operating.

BecomeHam.examProcessNote: Common-use stations, unlike individual ones, still need a licence.
